question: Phil Knight couldn’t sell encyclopaedias door to door. Why could he sell Japanese running shoes out of his car?
answer: Because, he decided, it wasn’t selling. He believed in running and in these shoes, and people sensed it and wanted some of that belief. A couple of sports shops had turned him away; at track meets across the Pacific Northwest he couldn’t write orders fast enough. In his words: ‘Belief is irresistible.’
move: Sell what you believe in; people can tell the difference.
simply: Imagine selling raffle tickets for a school trip you don’t care about, then for one you are dying to go on. The second time, your excitement does half the selling.
why: Most work involves persuading someone. Pitching something you doubt is tiring and it shows, while real conviction, backed by a product that delivers, carries much of the effort. Choosing what to sell may matter more than learning how to sell.
reference: Phil Knight, Shoe Dog: A Memoir by the Creator of Nike (Scribner, 2016), chapter ‘1964’
